Gates Industrial.why: Supplies data-center liquid-cooling components (hoses, quick disconnects, pumps); its data center business more than doubled year over year and is targeted at $100 million-$200 million of revenue by 2028
Gates Industrial.evidence: Gates Industrial Q2 FY2026 (07-31-2026), CEO Ivo Jurek: 'We continue to grow our data center business, which expanded more than 2x versus the prior year quarter'; 'our industrial water pumps that go in the applications in the data centers... ramping up our first sizable program with a major U.S.-based server manufacturer'

players.product: data-center liquid-cooling components: Data Master / Megaflex / Eco hoses, Universal Quick Disconnects (UQD), data center water pumps and supply-line couplings

quarterly_data.signal: Record quarterly sales of $942 million: total sales up 6.6% including currency benefits, core sales up 4.9%, near the high end of guidance; book-to-bill remained above one. Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $211 million (22.5% margin, modestly better than expected), adjusted gross margin up 50 basis points, and adjusted EPS rose 13% to a record $0.44. Power Transmission sales were $589 million (over 5% core growth); Fluid Power sales were $353 million (+4.2% core), with Fluid Power adjusted EBITDA margin down 120 basis points on footprint realignment costs and enterprise-initiative investments.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 sales $942 million (+6.6% total, +4.9% core); adj. EBITDA ~$211 million (22.5%); adj. EPS $0.44 (+13%)

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance raised: full-year core sales growth 2.5%-4.5% (+100 basis points at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA $800 million-$830 million (+$10 million at the midpoint) and adjusted EPS $1.62-$1.70 (+$0.06 at the midpoint); capex and free cash flow conversion guidance unchanged. Q3 revenue is guided to $880 million-$920 million with core revenue up approximately 5.5% at the midpoint and adjusted EBITDA margin up 50-90 basis points year over year. The updated guide implies 6% core growth in the second half versus approximately 1% in the first half, and management says it is on track for a second-half adjusted EBITDA margin of 23.5% or higher.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 core growth 2.5%-4.5%; adj. EBITDA $800 million-$830 million; adj. EPS $1.62-$1.70; Q3 revenue $880 million-$920 million; 2H adj. EBITDA margin 23.5%+

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ivo Jurek: the data center business 'expanded more than 2x versus the prior year quarter' and sales contribution is expected to step up in the second half 'as certain high-value project launches occur'. Data center is 'still a reasonably small level of revenue' but 'inflecting meaningfully'; 'we will be multiples of last year's revenue', and Gates anticipates $100 million-$200 million of data center revenue by 2028, which he says it has a high degree of confidence in delivering.
quarterly_data.figure: data center sales more than 2x YoY; $100 million-$200 million data center revenue anticipated by 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ivo Jurek: Gates is ramping revenue from its industrial water pumps used in data center applications and is 'now in process of actually ramping up our first sizable program with a major U.S.-based server manufacturer' (not named), expected to deliver 'a nice amount of incremental revenue' in the second half of 2026. Management also said it is 'ramping programs in support of our data center applications that we have been specified on'.

Management: Q2 bookings grew high single digits year over year, with that strength continuing through July, and Gates built 'a little bit of a backlog in Q2'; book-to-bill remained above one, giving a 'decent level of visibility' to the second-half trajectory embedded in guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 bookings up high single digits YoY; book-to-bill above one

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Brooks Mallard on price and cost: Gates implemented price increases to offset oil- and petroleum-related material cost increases (costs stable or slightly rising, no relief expected) and expects to be at least price-cost neutral in the second half; Q3 incremental margins are expected at 35%-40%, moving back to 45%+ in Q4. Footprint and cost optimization benefits are expected to roll through to the end of 2027. CEO: the 24.5% adjusted EBITDA margin target from the 2024 Capital Markets Day is how 'we are thinking about' it, is not 'some magic endpoint', and an update will come with the next CMD, likely in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 incrementals 35%-40%, Q4 45%+; 24.5% midterm adj. EBITDA margin target
